about: What the renderers of a drawing must agree on (docs/architecture/ink.md, The renderer). No renderer is normative: the data is the strokes, and the Swift one (CoreGraphics) and the web one (SVG) differ in antialiasing and in how many samples they take along a stroke. These tables are the part a viewer would notice: how much of its colour each kind of ink shows, which inks draw one width, which colour a name has, and what a name nobody knows is. `inks` maps an ink to its share of the colour (`alpha`, multiplied by each point's own opacity) and whether the stroke is drawn one width, the mean of its points'; an ink not listed, such as `airbrush`, is drawn like a pen. `marks` are the `<Mark>` hues, the same in every scheme. `ink` is the scheme's text colour, `accent` its brand colour, and a name that is not listed is drawn as ink.

darkStyle.about: How a fixed #rrggbb colour is drawn on a dark scheme: as PencilKit shows it in a dark interface style, the lightness of HSL reversed (1 - L) with hue and saturation kept, each channel rounded to the nearest of 255. Measured on the iPadOS 26.4 Simulator by drawing a stroke in a dark trait collection and reading its pixels; it matched this formula in every channel for 40 random colours and all seven inks. On a light scheme a fixed colour is as stored. [stored, shown on a dark scheme]
